subject: OrchidAI — Fleet sizing statement & burst-window profile
messages:
From: Sasha Ivanov <sasha@orchidai.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@orchidai.com>, Procurement <procurement@orchidai.com>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: OrchidAI — initial traffic snapshot for Dedicated sizing

Hi Jonas / Camila,

Thanks for the demo last week. Per our procurement and infra leads, we're trying to lock down the sizing worksheet for a Dedicated reserved plan. Attached is a CSV with a 7-day sample of production requests (anonymized): timestamp, model_variant, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, duration_ms, customer_region.

High level asks from our side:
- We expect a baseline of ~220 qps during business hours (US-PST) with 3 short burst windows per day up to ~1,400 qps for 3–8 minutes.
- Average prompt length: 120 tokens, typical completion 350 tokens; roughly 85% of traffic is retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with KV-cache benefit.
- P95 latency target is 600ms for synchronous requests; anything beyond starts breaking our user experience.

Can you confirm what fleet mix and oversubscription assumptions you'd recommend, and whether Redwood can guarantee fallbacks to a lower-cost quantized variant during sustained bursts?

Also copying procurement for contract lead time.

Thanks,
Sasha
Head of Infrastructure, OrchidAI

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Ivanov <sasha@orchidai.com>, Ops Team <ops@orchidai.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2029 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OrchidAI — initial traffic snapshot for Dedicated sizing

Sasha — really helpful sample, thanks. Quick responses below and next steps:  

1) Baseline vs burst: the pattern you describe (220 qps baseline, 3 bursts/day to ~1.4k qps) maps well to a hybrid allocation: a reserved baseline fleet sized for sustained throughput + burst pool assigned via autoscale with a predictable ramp. We'll sketch both conservative and aggressive commitment options.

2) Token profile: your average and completion token counts suggest a per-request median of ~470 tokens. For RAG workloads we assume ~20–30% KV-cache hit for prefix stability in typical embeddings pipelines — please confirm if you use sticky sessions for retrieval.

3) Latency: 600ms p95 synchronous is achievable at modest cost if we prioritize single-request latency (lower batching) and use smaller sequence-optimized kernels. We'll include a p95/cost tradeoff table.

Action items:
- Camila will produce a "2-option" sizing workbook (Conservative: 25% headroom; Aggressive: 10% headroom + faster recovery) with GPU SKUs and estimated monthly unit cost.
- Marissa will run a quick simulator using your CSV to estimate concurrency and KV cache hit sensitivity.
- Please confirm whether you require HSM/KMS integration for key material — affects private deployment timelines.

I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up next Tue to review the workbook.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Ivanov <sasha@orchidai.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2029 11:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OrchidAI — initial traffic snapshot for Dedicated sizing

Sasha / team — attaching the workbook draft (SLA-burst-matrix.xlsx) and a short notes sheet. Highlights below:  

- Conservative option: 12 x A100 80GB-equivalent GPUs, reserved baseline capacity to handle sustained 220 qps with 25% buffer; burst served by 6x pre-warmed surge nodes (same SKU) + autoscale to add ephemeral nodes up to full burst.
- Aggressive option: 8 x H100 80GB-equivalent with higher per-GPU throughput, smaller headroom (10%), faster cold-start recovery; assumes aggressive quantization path for fallback.
- Estimated token economics: conservative ~ $0.076 per 1k generated tokens; aggressive ~ $0.062 per 1k with quantized variants. These include network and storage overheads.

Open questions:  
- Do you want transparent canary routing (traffic % by route) versus all-or-nothing cutovers? We recommend staged canaries to validate RAG quality.
- Any regulatory retention constraints that require on-prem or VPC-only deployment?

Attachment stub: sla-burst-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Cheers,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sasha Ivanov <sasha@orchidai.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@orchidai.com>, Procurement <procurement@orchidai.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2029 10:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OrchidAI — initial traffic snapshot for Dedicated sizing

Camila — thanks for the workbook and notes. Quick clarifications:  

- We do sticky sessions in the retrieval layer for ~40% of RAG calls, so KV-cache hit should be higher than your 20–30% assumption — closer to 45% in the dataset periods. I'll mark that in the sample and re-send a trimmed CSV.
- We require KMS integration (AWS KMS) and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM; on-prem is not required for initial commit.
- Procurement asked for an explicit SLA exception clause for burst-related throttling and a short fallback appendix describing the quantized model quality guarantees.

Next step: I'll upload the revised CSV and procurement checklist to your Drive link by EOD Wed. Planning to join Tue's review if the time works.

—Sasha

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Ivanov <sasha@orchidai.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2029 16:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OrchidAI — initial traffic snapshot for Dedicated sizing

Sasha — received the updated note and CSV (thanks). I ran a short simulator with the 45% KV-cache hit and sticky-session distribution. Key findings:  

- With 45% cache, the conservative plan could drop to 10 x A100-equivalents while still maintaining p95 < 600ms for baseline and handling two of the three daily bursts without exceeding autoscale cold-start budget.
- For full three-burst coverage with <= 30s recovery to peak, the aggressive H100 plan is the better fit (reduces cold-start exposure and per-token cost by ~18%).
- Fallback behavior: we can commit to an explicit burst-fallback appendix in the contract that defines acceptable quality degradation metrics (ROUGE/Embeddings distance thresholds) for the quantized variant; we will require a 30-day joint validation run before contract signature.

Attachments referenced: orchid_token_samples.csv (text/csv), redwood-dedicated-outline.pdf (application/pdf)

Next concrete: I'll post a final two-option workbook in the Drive by tomorrow morning and set the Tue review for 2029-05-28 10:00 PT unless you prefer an earlier slot. HubSpot deal link: https://hubspot.example/deal/ORC-2029-EXP-09

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
